The connection URL tells Grafana where to send log queries. The format depends on your Loki environment.

Use the URL format that matches your backend:

| Environment | URL format | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Self-managed Loki | `http://<host>:3100` | `http://loki:3100` |
| Grafana Cloud Logs | `https://logs-prod-<zone>.grafana.net` | `https://logs-prod-006.grafana.net` |
| Grafana Enterprise Logs | URL of your GEL gateway | `https://gel.example.com` |

To configure the connection URL, complete the following step:

In the **URL** field under the **Connection** section, enter the query URL for your Loki backend.

For example, for Grafana Cloud Logs, enter a URL like `https://logs-prod-006.grafana.net`. For self-managed Loki, enter a URL like `http://loki:3100`.

**Tip:** The URLs above are for **querying** logs from Grafana. To send logs *to* Loki, refer to [Send log data to Loki](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/send-data/).
In the next milestone, you configure authentication for the connection.
